- Extract the complete new-physics content of arXiv:2311.18472 (NJLComposite model) into `spec.json` (FeynRulesModel JSON only, `model_name = "NJLComposite_gen"`), then run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate until lint findings are fixed per TASK.md's TOOLKIT section; final message must follow TASK.md's ending instruction (tail beyond "Your final message: the" may still be truncated — re-read from offset ~14).

## Important Details
- Working dir: `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-NJLComposite-zxkbktvj/` — work only inside it.
- Shell restricted: only `./frgen *` / `./frgen` allowed (all other bash denied). Use read/grep/write tools for everything else.
- Schema rules: numeric values are strings ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups: []`; standard indices (Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W) need no declaration; other indices need `index_decls` (range_kind "NoUnfold"); unique `class_index` ≥ 100; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields.
- Scoring: COMPLETENESS of new particles, External parameters, verbatim Mathematica `lagrangian_terms`.
- Lint/root-cause findings from first `./frgen spec.json` run (13 findings):
  - `explicit_index_in_dc` (warn, 6× scalars): `DC[PI1bar[ii],mu]` etc. — fix by writing `ExpandIndices[DC[PI1bar, mu] DC[PI1, mu] - mPi^2 PI1bar[ii] PI1[ii], FlavorExpand->SU2D]` (no explicit index inside DC). Affects PI1, PI2, Hc1, Hc2, LQ1, LQ2 (model.fr lines 379–389).
  - `fieldless_term` (mg5) on `LFCI` (model.fr line 423): linter's `field_tokens` = class_names | class_name+"bar" | SM_FIELDS_ALL | bare ClassMembers (members get NO "bar" suffix added). SM_FIELDS_ALL comes from `~/Documents/Github/heptapod/tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr` which likely doesn't exist locally → empty. LFCI uses only `FU0bar`, `FUpb`, `FE23bar`, etc. → no match. Fix: rewrite LFCI using proper class fields with explicit SU2 indices, e.g. `FU1bar[sp1,1,ff,cc]`, `FD1bar[sp2,1,gg,cc]` (component 1 = U0/D0, component 2 = U−/D−; `FUpb`=bar of FUm=`FU1bar[...,2,...]`, `FDpb`=`FD1bar[...,2,...]`).
  - `undeclared_symbol QL` (warn, in LYPI/LYLQ/LHcFF): false positive — lint checks only capitalised identifiers used with `[`/`.` against external heptapod SM.fr (missing locally); local SM.fr declares `QL`.
  - `undeclared_symbol FUpb` (warn, LFCI): real — FUpb is not a class/member field name; use `FU1bar` with index.
  - `undeclared_symbol Eqs` (warn, LANOMPI0/LANOMPIc): real — prose "Sum over..."/"Eqs.(PiGG)" inside expressions; must be pure Mathematica (move prose to description).
- Lint's fieldless/undeclared logic (from `tools/fr_lint.py`): `term_defs` stops at `^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)`; undeclared check only fires for identifiers starting uppercase used with `[` or `.`; `FR_SYMBOLS`/`PROTECTED` name-collision sets; `sm_couplings = {"ee","gw","gs","g1","yl","yu","yd","lam","CKM"}`.
- Paper physics (authoritative lines read): contact Yukawa Eqs. (ciqlB–iqlBuql, tex lines 488–501): gY( d̄_R u_L )Π− + h.c. etc.; composite-fermion contact (cieFf0+ etc., tex lines 818–831): V = (g*²/Λ²)(Ū⁰_L u^a_R)(ū^a_R ν_L) + h.c. and analogues for U+, D+, D0; Π quantum numbers Table (tex 353–367): Π+ Q=+1 t3=+1/2 Y=+1/2; Π− Y=−1/2; Π0u t3=+1/2 Y=−1/2; Π0d t3=−1/2 Y=+1/2; anomaly vertices gg'N_c/(4π²F_Π)ε(∂A)(∂A')Π0,Π± (tex ~922–941).
- Design decisions in spec: two complex SU2 doublets for Π (PI1, PI2) despite Π−=(Π+†) ambiguity; Mass specs carry mPi/MF/MN (so those names absent from M$Parameters); parameters: Lam (5100.), FPi (1000.), gY Internal "(FPi/Lam)^2", gYp (0.1), gst (1.); `interaction_order_hierarchy [["QCD",1],["QED",2],["NP",1]]`.
- Naming constraints: avoid SM.fr/FR-symbol collisions (`Pi`, `N`, `D`, `E`, `HC`, `DC`, ...) — hence PI1/Hc1/FN1 style; no primes/punctuation in ParticleName.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read TASK.md (to line 14), `frmodel.py`, `render.py`, `fr_lint.py`, `model.fr.j2`, `SM.fr`, `frgen` wrapper; fully read paper tex (lines 1–600, 601–1200, 1201–1750, 1735–end).
- Wrote complete first `spec.json`: 19 particle classes (PI1, PI2, Hc1, Hc2, LQ1, LQ2, FN1, FE1, FNs, FEs, FN2, FE2, FNsC, FEsC, FU1, FD1, FUsC, FDsC, nur); 5 parameters; 26 lagrangian_terms.
- First `./frgen spec.json` run succeeded: SCHEMA OK (19 classes, 5 params, 26 terms), RENDERED `model.fr` (429 lines), LINT reported 13 findings (all `warn` except one `mg5`).
- Diagnosed root causes of all 13 lint findings (see Important Details).

### Active
- Fixing the 13 lint findings by editing `spec.json` (not yet edited).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Edit `spec.json` to fix lint findings: (a) remove explicit indices from DC[...] in the 6 scalar kinetic terms; (b) rewrite `LFCI` using class fields with explicit SU2 indices (`FU1bar[...,1/2,...]`, `FD1bar[...]`, member fields via class names) so fields are recognized and `FUpb` disappears; (c) strip prose from `LANOMPI0`/`LANOMPIc` bodies (pure Mathematica, e.g. `gQ2 Nc/(4 Pi^2 FPi)` with `gQ2`/`Nc` handled — move prose to `description`); (d) optionally restructure `LYPI`/`LYLQ`/`LHcFF` QL usage if deemed real (likely false positive from missing external heptapod SM.fr).
2. Re-run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until findings are only harmless warns.
3. Re-read TASK.md tail (offset ~14) for final-message requirement; produce final message with self-audit tables (per-term Q/Y sums, coupling dimensions, completeness list).

## Relevant Files
- `TASK.md`: authoritative instructions; tail past "Your final message: the" possibly still truncated (re-read from offset ~14).
- `paper/2311.18472_source.tex`: authoritative paper LaTeX (fully read; key regions 350–501, 800–941).
- `spec.json`: current model spec; needs lint fixes.
- `model.fr`: rendered output (429 lines); findings reference lines 379–423.
- `tools/fr_lint.py`: lint rules — root causes of all 13 findings.
- `tools/frgen/frmodel.py`, `tools/frgen/render.py`, `tools/frgen/templates/model.fr.j2`: schema/renderer.
- `SM.fr`: local baseline SM (has `QL`, `uR`, `eR`, `dq`, `vl`, etc.); name-collision reference.
- `frgen`: wrapper script; only allowed shell command (`./frgen spec.json`).
Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed.

10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import json
22: import re
23: import sys
24: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
25: from pathlib import Path
26: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
27: 
28: HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
29: SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"
30: 
31: # Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}
39: 
40: # Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
42: SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
43: SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
44: for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
45:     SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
46: _i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
47: SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
48: SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
49: SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
50:               "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
51: SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
52: SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
53:              "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}
54: 
55: FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
56:                "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
57:                "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
58:                "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
59:                "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
60:                "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
61:                "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
62:                "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
63:                "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
64:                "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}

66: 
67: @dataclass
68: class Finding:
69:     rule: str
70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None
73: 
74: 
75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1
109: 
110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None
157: 
158: 
159: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- lints
160: 
161: def lint_text(raw: str) -> List[Finding]:
162:     text = strip_comments(raw)
163:     F: List[Finding] = []
164:     classes = _entries(_block(text, "ClassesDescription"))
165:     params = _entries(_block(text, "Parameters"))
166:     terms = term_defs(text)
167:     term_names = {t["name"] for t in terms}
168:     term_bodies = "\n".join(t["body"] for t in terms)
169: 
170:     class_names, class_idx = {}, {}
171:     for c in classes:
172:         cn = _prop(c["body"], "ClassName")
173:         if cn:
174:             class_names[cn] = c
175:             mi = re.match(r"(\w+)\[\s*(\d+)\s*\]", c["head"])
176:             if mi:
177:                 class_idx[cn] = (mi.group(1), int(mi.group(2)))
178:     param_names = {p["head"]: p for p in params}
179:     index_decls = dict(re.findall(r"IndexRange\[\s*Index\[(\w+)\]\s*\]\s*=\s*([^;\n]+)", text))
180: 
181:     # --- rule 10: names -------------------------------------------------
182:     for name in list(class_names) + list(param_names) + list(index_decls):
183:         if name in FR_SYMBOLS:
184:             F.append(Finding("feynrules_symbol_name", "compile",
185:                              f"`{name}` is a FeynRules symbol", _line_of(text, name)))
186:         elif name in PROTECTED:
187:             F.append(Finding("protected_name", "warn",
188:                              f"`{name}` is a Mathematica built-in (loads with a warning; renaming is safer)",
189:                              _line_of(text, name)))
190:     for name in class_names:
191:         if name in SM_CLASSES or name in SM_MEMBERS:
192:             F.append(Finding("sm_class_redeclared", "warn",
193:                              f"class `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr (doubly-defined class)",
194:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {name}")))
195:     for name in param_names:
196:         if name in SM_PARAMS or name in SM_MASSES:
197:             F.append(Finding("sm_parameter_redeclared", "warn",
198:                              f"parameter `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr", _line_of(text, name)))
199:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
200:         for key in ("ParticleName", "AntiParticleName"):
201:             v = _prop(c["body"], key)
202:             names = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', v) if v else []
203:             if v and any(re.search(r"[\'`\s!@#%^&*()=\[\]{}|\\;:<>?/,]", nm) for nm in names):
204:                 F.append(Finding("bad_particle_name", "mg5",
205:                                  f"class `{cn}`: {key} {v} is not a valid UFO identifier", _line_of(text, v)))
206:         if cn in class_idx and class_idx[cn][1] < 100:
207:             F.append(Finding("low_class_index", "warn",
208:                              f"class `{cn}` uses index {class_idx[cn][0]}[{class_idx[cn][1]}]; SM.fr uses the low indices",
209:                              _line_of(text, c["head"])))
210:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
211:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
212:                 if mem in SM_MEMBERS or mem in SM_CLASSES:
213:                     F.append(Finding("sm_member_redeclared", "compile",
214:                                      f"class member `{mem}` of `{cn}` collides with an SM.fr name",
215:                                      _line_of(text, mem)))
216:     if "$" in re.sub(r"M\$\w+", "", text):
217:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b\w*\$\w*", text):
218:             if not re.match(r"^(M|MR|FR)\$", m.group(0)):
219:                 F.append(Finding("dollar_in_name", "mg5", f"`{m.group(0)}` contains `$` (invalid Python)",
220:                                  text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1))
221:                 break
222: 
223:     # --- rule 11: interaction orders --------------------------------------
224:     hierarchy = _block(text, "InteractionOrderHierarchy")
225:     orders_declared = set(re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*-?\d+\s*\}", hierarchy))
226:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
227:         body = p["body"]
228:         ptype = (_prop(body, "ParameterType") or "External").strip()
229:         io = _prop(body, "InteractionOrder")
230:         used = re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", term_bodies) is not None
231:         is_mass = any(re.search(rf"Mass\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"]) or
232:                       re.search(rf"Width\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"])
233:                       for c in classes) or re.match(r"^(M|W)[A-Z]", pn) and not io
234:         if io:
235:             oname = re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,", io)
236:             for o in oname:
237:                 if o not in orders_declared and o not in ("QCD", "QED"):
238:                     F.append(Finding("order_not_in_hierarchy", "warn",
239:                                      f"parameter `{pn}` uses InteractionOrder `{o}` not listed in M$InteractionOrderHierarchy",
240:                                      _line_of(text, pn)))
241:     ordered = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items() if _prop(p["body"], "InteractionOrder")}
242:     internal = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items()
243:                 if (_prop(p["body"], "ParameterType") or "External").strip() == "Internal"}
244:     # an Internal parameter inherits the orders of the parameters in its Value
245:     for pn in list(internal):
246:         val = _prop(param_names[pn]["body"], "Value") or ""
247:         if any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(o)}\b", val) for o in ordered):
248:             ordered.add(pn)
249:     for t in terms:
250:         if _is_kin_name(t["name"]):
251:             continue
252:         used_params = {pn for pn in param_names if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", t["body"])}
253:         sm_couplings = {"ee", "gw", "gs", "g1", "yl", "yu", "yd", "lam", "CKM"}
254:         if used_params and not (used_params & ordered) and not \
255:                 any(re.search(rf"\b{c}\b", t["body"]) for c in sm_couplings) and \
256:                 not any(re.search(rf"\b(DC|FS)\[", t["body"]) for _ in [0]):
257:             F.append(Finding("missing_interaction_order", "mg5",
258:                              f"`{t['name']}`: none of its parameters ({', '.join(sorted(used_params))}) carries an InteractionOrder",
259:                              t["line"]))
260: 
261:     # --- rule 12: pattern rules on tensor parameters -----------------------
262:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
263:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:?->", p["body"]) or "_?NumericQ" in p["body"]:
264:             F.append(Finding("pattern_rule_definition", "mg5",
265:                              f"parameter `{pn}` uses a pattern rule in Definitions/Value; FeynRules exports it verbatim as a UFO name",
266:                              _line_of(text, pn)))
267:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
268:         d = _prop(c["body"], "Definitions") or ""
269:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:>", d) and not re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_\s*[,\]]", d):
270:             pass  # `X[mu_] :> ...` is the normal FeynRules idiom; leave it
271: 
272:     # --- rule 13: explicit indices ------------------------------------------
273:     for t in terms:
274:         b = t["body"]
275:         for m in re.finditer(r"DC\[\s*(\w+)\[([^\]]*)\]\s*,", b):
276:             fld = m.group(1)
277:             c = class_names.get(fld)
278:             idx = (_prop(c["body"], "Indices") or "") if c else ""
279:             if c and re.search(r"Colour|Sextet|Gluon|Octet|Col", idx):
280:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "compile",
281:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on `{fld}` with an explicit colour-type index", t["line"]))
282:             else:
283:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "warn",
284:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on an explicitly indexed field `{fld}`", t["line"]))
285:             break
286:         if re.search(r"Index\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]\s*,\s*Index\[\s*Generation", b) or \
287:                 re.search(r"\w+\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]", b):
288:             F.append(Finding("nested_generation_index", "compile",
289:                              f"`{t['name']}`: nested generation index", t["line"]))
290:         m = re.search(r"\b(\w+)\[\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|ii\d?)\s*,\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|jj\d?)\s*\]\s*\w+bar\[", b)
291:         if m and m.group(1) in param_names:
292:             F.append(Finding("explicit_flavour_sum", "mg5",
293:                              f"`{t['name']}`: flavour matrix `{m.group(1)}` with explicit generation indices instead of matrix form",
294:                              t["line"]))
295: 
296:     # --- rule 14: one declared total ---------------------------------------
297:     roots = []
298:     for t in terms:
299:         if not any(re.search(rf"\b{t['name']}\b", u["body"]) for u in terms if u is not t):
300:             roots.append(t["name"])
301:     if terms and not roots:
302:         F.append(Finding("no_total_lagrangian", "harness", "no Lagrangian symbol is a root (circular or empty)", None))
303:     elif len(roots) > 1:
304:         F.append(Finding("ambiguous_total", "harness",
305:                          f"{len(roots)} root Lagrangian symbols: {', '.join(roots)}", None))
306:     elif roots and roots[0] not in ("LTotal", "LTot", "LFull", "LBSM", "LNP", "Lag", "LagTot"):
307:         F.append(Finding("total_not_named_ltotal", "warn", f"the single root is `{roots[0]}`, not LTotal", None))
308:     field_tokens = set(class_names) | {c + "bar" for c in class_names} | SM_FIELDS_ALL
309:     for c in classes:
310:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
311:             field_tokens |= {x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()}
312:     for t in terms:
313:         rhs = t["body"].split("=", 1)[-1]
314:         if re.search(r"\bL\w+\b", rhs) and any(re.search(rf"\b{u['name']}\b", rhs) for u in terms if u is not t):
315:             continue  # a sum of other terms
316:         if not any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(f)}\b", rhs) for f in field_tokens):
317:             F.append(Finding("fieldless_term", "mg5", f"`{t['name']}` contains no field", t["line"]))
318: 
319:     # --- rule 15: declarations -----------------------------------------------
320:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
321:         sc = (_prop(c["body"], "SelfConjugate") or "").strip()
322:         qn = _prop(c["body"], "QuantumNumbers")
323:         if sc == "True" and qn and re.search(r"->\s*-?[1-9]", qn):
324:             F.append(Finding("selfconjugate_with_qn", "warn",
325:                              f"class `{cn}` is SelfConjugate and carries QuantumNumbers {qn}",
326:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {cn}")))
327:         if sc == "True" and _prop(c["body"], "AntiParticleName"):
328:             pass
329:     # Majorana mass normalisation
330:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
331:         if (_prop(c["body"], "SelfConjugate") or "").strip() == "True" and c["head"].startswith("F"):
332:             mm = re.search(r"Mass\s*->\s*\{\s*(\w+)", c["body"])
333:             if not mm:
334:                 continue
335:             M = mm.group(1)
336:             pat = re.compile(rf"(-?\s*(?:1/2|0\.5|\(1/2\))?\s*\*?\s*{M}\b[^;]{{0,40}}{cn}bar\s*\.\s*{cn}\b)")
337:             for t in terms:
338:                 for hit in pat.finditer(t["body"]):
339:                     if not re.search(r"1/2|0\.5", hit.group(1)):
340:                         F.append(Finding("majorana_mass_no_half", "checks",
341:                                          f"`{t['name']}`: Majorana mass term for `{cn}` without the 1/2",
342:                                          t["line"]))
343:     # undeclared symbols in terms (conservative: capitalised identifiers used as fields)
344:     declared = set(class_names) | {c + "bar" for c in class_names} | set(param_names) | \
345:         SM_FIELDS_ALL | SM_PARAMS | SM_MASSES | FR_BUILTINS | set(term_names) | set(index_decls) | \
346:         {"If", "Which", "Table", "KroneckerDelta", "Transpose", "Inverse", "ArcTan", "Sec", "Csc",
347:          "Cot", "Abs", "MatrixExp", "DiagonalMatrix", "IdentityMatrix", "Sum", "Product"}
348:     for c in classes:
349:         for key in ("Mass", "Width"):
350:             v = _prop(c["body"], key) or ""
351:             declared |= set(re.findall(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", v)) - {"Internal", "External", "Automatic"}
352:     for c in classes:
353:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
354:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
355:                 declared |= {mem, mem + "bar"}
356:         for m in re.finditer(r"Unphysical\s*->\s*True", c["body"]):
357:             pass
358:     for t in terms:
359:         b = re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', "", t["body"])
360:         locals_ = set()
361:         for m in re.finditer(r"(?:Block|Module)\[\s*\{([^}]*)\}", b):
362:             locals_ |= {x.strip().split("=")[0].strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",")}
363:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", b):
364:             s = m.group(1)
365:             if s in declared or s in locals_ or s == t["name"] or len(s) < 2:
366:                 continue
367:             if re.match(r"^(mu|nu|rho|sig|la|lam|al|be|sp|ss|ii|jj|kk|ll|ff|gg|cc|aa|bb|tt|rr|xx|yy|zz)\d*$", s):
368:                 continue
369:             if s in ("ExpandIndices", "FlavorExpand", "Index", "Sqrt", "HC"):
370:                 continue
371:             if s[0].isupper() and re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(s)}\s*[\[.]", b):
372:                 F.append(Finding("undeclared_symbol", "warn",
373:                                  f"`{t['name']}` uses `{s}` which is neither declared here nor by SM.fr",
374:                                  t["line"]))
375:                 break
376: 
377:     # --- rule 9: non-fundamental colour representations -----------------------
378:     for iname, rng in index_decls.items():
379:         if re.search(r"Range\[\s*6\s*\]", rng) and "AddGaugeRepresentation" not in text:
380:             F.append(Finding("sextet_without_representation", "warn",
381:                              f"index `{iname}` has range 6 but there is no AddGaugeRepresentation", _line_of(text, iname)))
382: 
383:     # --- mass mixing written into Definitions (the dominant check failure) ----
384:     phys_new = {cn for cn, c in class_names.items() if (_prop(c["body"], "Unphysical") or "").strip() != "True"}
385:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
386:         d = _prop(c["body"], "Definitions") or ""
387:         if not d:
388:             continue
389:         fields_in = {s for s in re.findall(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", d) if s in phys_new or s in SM_CLASSES}
390:         fields_in -= {cn}
391:         if len(fields_in) >= 2 and re.search(r"\b(sa|ca|sin|cos|Sin|Cos|s\w*|c\w*)\w*\b", d):
392:             F.append(Finding("mixing_in_definitions", "checks",
393:                              f"class `{cn}` is defined as a mixture of {sorted(fields_in)}; the mass basis of the partner fields declared in SM.fr is unchanged",
394:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {cn}")))
395:     return F
396: 
397: 
398: def lint_file(path: str) -> List[Finding]:
399:     return lint_text(Path(path).read_text(errors="replace"))
400: 
401: 
402: if __name__ == "__main__":
403:     for p in sys.argv[1:]:
404:         fs = lint_file(p)
405:         print(json.dumps({"file": p, "findings": [asdict(f) for f in fs]}, indent=1))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the

808: \section{contact interaction of composite fermions}
809: 
810: The contact interactions for the production and decay of a

812: \begin{eqnarray}

819: \label{cieFf0+}\\

821: \label{cinuFf0+}\\
822: {\mathcal V}_{\bar D^+} &=& \frac{g_*^2}{\Lambda^2}(\bar D^+_{L}d^a_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}e_{L}),
823: \quad pp~\rightarrow \bar D^+_{L}e_{L}; \quad ep~\rightarrow \bar D^+_{L}d^a_{R},
824: \label{cieF0+}\\

828: and their Hermitian conjugates,
829: \begin{eqnarray}

831: \label{dcieFf0+}\\

873: \subsection{Contact interaction of $\Pi^{0,\pm}$ composite boson and gauge bosons}\label{spgg}
874: 
875: However, we shall consider other decay channels at the next leading order, such as neutral composite boson decay to two SM gauge bosons $\Pi^0_{u,d}\rightarrow \tilde G + \tilde G'$. We need a figure for $\Pi \rightarrow \tilde G + \tilde G'$. 
876: Note that the discussions here in this section do not apply to LQ composite bosons $\Pi^Q_a$ at this leading order, because that SM gauge bosons are zero or integer electric charges and the fractionally charged LQ composite bosons cannot decay to SM gauge bosons. \red{
877: The composite bosons $\Pi^{0,\pm}$ have two components: the pesudo scalar and scalar component. As example $\Pi^+=(g^*/F_\Pi)^2(\bar d^a_{R}u_{La})$ (\ref{nB0}) and $\Pi^0_u=(g^*/F_\Pi)^2(\bar u^a_{R}u_{La})$ (\ref{uB0}) are \cite{xue2017} 
878: \begin{eqnarray}
879: \Pi^+ &=&(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\bar d^a\frac{(1-\gamma_5)}{2}u_{a}= (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar d^au_{a}-\bar d^a\gamma_5u_{a}\Big)\label{twocomp+}\\
880: \Pi^0_u &=&(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\bar u^a\frac{(1-\gamma_5)}{2}u_{a}= (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar u^au_{a}-\bar u^a\gamma_5u_{a}\Big),
881: \label{twocomp0u}\\
882: \Pi^0_d &=&(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\bar d^a\frac{(1-\gamma_5)}{2}d_{a}= (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar d^ad_{a}-\bar d^a\gamma_5d_{a}\Big),
883: \label{twocomp0d}
884: \end{eqnarray}
885: which can be generalized to the 2nd and 3rd generations. In the following studies of composite bosons decaying to two SM gauge bosons via a fermion loop,
886: for the sake of notations, we use the $\Pi^{0,\pm}$ also for the pseudoscalar component with $\gamma_5$ presence, and introduce Higg-like ${\rm H}^{0,\pm}$ for  scalar component without $\gamma_5$ presence. Namely, henceforth, for pseudoscalar composite bosons
887: \begin{eqnarray}
888: \Pi^+ &=& (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar d^a\gamma_5u_{a}\Big)\label{twocomp+}\\
889: \Pi^0_u &=& (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar u^a\gamma_5u_{a}\Big),
890: \label{twocomp0u}\\
891: \Pi^0_d &=& (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar d^a\gamma_5d_{a}\Big),
892: \label{twocomp0d}
893: \end{eqnarray}
894: and for scalar Higg-like ${\rm H}^{0,\pm}$ bosons
895: \begin{eqnarray}
896: {\rm H}^+ &=& (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar d^au_{a}\Big)\label{htwocomp+}\\
897: {\rm H}^0_u &=& (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar u^au_{a}\Big),
898: \label{htwocomp0u}\\
899: {\rm H}^0_d &=& (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar d^ad_{a}\Big).
900: \label{htwocomp0d}
901: \end{eqnarray}
902: These can be generalized to the 2nd and 3rd families, ${\rm H}^0_t = (1/2)(g^*/F_\Pi)^2\Big(\bar t^at_{a}\Big)$ can be the candidate of the second Higgs particle, a massive and tightly bound state.}
903: 
904: Analogously to $\pi^0\rightarrow \gamma\gamma$, the massive $\Pi^0_{u,d}$ composite boson (pesudo scalar component) can also decay into two gauge bosons \cite{xue2017} :
905: \begin{eqnarray}
906: \Pi^0_{u,d} &\rightarrow& \gamma +\gamma, \label{cpg}\\
907: \Pi^0_{u,d} &\rightarrow& \gamma +Z^0,\label{cpgz} \\
908: \Pi^0_{u,d} &\rightarrow& Z^0 + Z^0, \label{cpzz} \\
909: \Pi^0_{u,d} &\rightarrow& W^+ + W^-,\label{cpww}
910: \end{eqnarray}
911: via the contact interaction
912: \begin{eqnarray}
913: {\mathcal L}^{\Pi^0}_{\tilde G\tilde G'} = \sum_{i=u,d}\frac{ gg^\prime N_c}{4\pi^2
914: F_\Pi}\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}(\partial^\rho A^\mu)(\partial^\sigma A^{\prime\nu})\Pi^0_i,
915: \label{PiGG} 
916: \end{eqnarray}
917: where $g$ and $g^\prime$ represent the 
918: couplings of gauge bosons $A^\mu$ and $A^{\prime\nu}$ to the SM quarks $u$ 
919: and $d$ with different $SU_L(2)$-isospin $i=u,d$. 
920: Actually, this effective contact 
921: interaction (\ref{PiGG})
922: is an axial anomaly vertex, as a result of a triangle quark loop and standard renormalization procedure in SM. The color factor $N_c=3$ comes from the trace over color space of quarks in loop. The contact interaction (\ref{PiGG}) can be written as 
923: \begin{eqnarray}
924: {\mathcal L}^{\Pi^0}_{\tilde G\tilde G'} = \sum_{i=u,d}\frac{ gg^\prime N_c}{4\pi^2
925: F_\Pi}\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\frac{1}{4}(F^{\rho\mu})(F^{\prime\sigma\nu})\Pi^0_i.
926: \label{PiGG1} 
927: \end{eqnarray}
928: \red{These amplitudes or effective interacting Lagrangians are the same, independent of quark types and masses in triangle loop. Therefore, it is the same and generalized for all generations. In addition, $\Pi^0_{u,d}$ decay to two gluons
929: \begin{eqnarray}
930: \Pi^0_{u,d} &\rightarrow& \tilde g
931: + \tilde g,\label{cpgg}
932: \end{eqnarray}
933: via the contact interaction
934: \begin{eqnarray}
935: {\mathcal L}^{\Pi^0}_{\tilde g\tilde g'} &=& \sum_{i=u,d}\frac{ g_s^2/2}{4\pi^2
936: F_\Pi}\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}(\partial^\rho A^\mu_a)(\partial^\sigma A^{\prime\nu}_a)\Pi^0_i\nonumber\\
937: &=& \sum_{i=u,d}\frac{ g_s^2/2}{4\pi^2
938: F_\Pi}\epsilon_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}\frac{1}{4}(G^{\rho\mu}_a)(G^{\prime\sigma\nu}_a)\Pi^0_i,
939: \label{PiGGg} 
940: \end{eqnarray}
941: where the strong coupling $g_s$ and $\alpha_s=g_s^2/(4\pi)$, the trace over color space gives $\tr(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2$, leading to $(G^{\rho\mu}_a)(G^{\prime\sigma\nu}_a)$ summed over color index $a$, see Ref.~\cite{anomalyS}.

Thus their triangle diagram contributions to the anomaly, i.e., $\pi^0$ decays to two gluons, are the same, but opposite in sign, therefore exactly canceled each other. As a result, the total amplitude of the normal $\pi^0$ decay to two gluons is zero. This is not the case for its decay to two photons, since the $u$ and $d$ have different electric charges. In our case, $\Pi^0_u$ and $\Pi^0_d$ are different states, and both decay to two gluons and amplitudes are the same.}

482: \subsection{Contact interaction of composite bosons, quarks and leptons}\label{spqq}
483: 
484: As shown in Fig.~\ref{compositeBv}, 
485: the effective coupling between composite boson 
486: and its two constituents can be written as an effective contact interaction, 
487: \begin{eqnarray}
488: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^\pm}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar d^a_{R}u_{La})\Pi^- + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlB}\\
489: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_d}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar d^a_{R} d_{La})\Pi^0_d + {\rm h.c.},
490: \label{iqlBd}\\
491: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_u}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar u^a_{R} u_{La})\Pi^0_u + {\rm h.c.},
492: \label{iqlBu}
493: \end{eqnarray}
494: and 
495: \begin{eqnarray}
496: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{+5/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R}u_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql}\\
497: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{-1/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar\nu^e_{R}d_{La})\Pi^{-1/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql1}\\
498: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar \nu^e_{R}u_{La}) \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a} + {\rm h.c.},
499: \label{iqlBuql}\\
500: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{d_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R} d_{La})\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a} + {\rm h.c.},
501: \label{iqlBdql}
502: \end{eqnarray}
503: where $g_{_{\rm Y}}=(F_\Pi/\Lambda)^2$.
504: Appropriate normalizing the composite boson $\Pi$ with the 
505: form factor $(g^*/F_\Pi)^2$ in Eqs. (\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}),  
506: the effective contact interaction in Eqs. (\ref{ciqlB}-\ref{iqlBu}) and (\ref{ciqlBql}-\ref{iqlBdql}) can be expressed as a dimensionless Yukawa coupling $g_{_{\rm Y}}$, 
507: whose value, corresponding to $F_\Pi$ value, 
508: can be different for composite bosons in Eqs.~(\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}) and (\ref{nB5/3}-\ref{uB2/3}), but we do not consider such difference here.
509: These are relevant contact interactions for phenomenological studies of possible inelastic channels of composite-fermion production and decay in  $pp$ or $ep$ collisions.
510: 
511: \red{We discuss the issue of generation mixing for four different charged types of LQ states: $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}$, $\Pi^{-1/3}_{a}$  $\Pi^{2/3}_{u_a}$ and $\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a}$ in Table \ref{qnuP0ql}. Each type has three copies due to generations, taking as example $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}\sim (\bar e_{R}u_{La})$, $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}\sim (\bar \mu_{R}c_{La})$ and $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}\sim (\bar \tau_{R}t_{La})$. If the LQ $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}$ is produced by, then decay to its constituents in the same generation, the Yukawa coupling $g_Y\sim {\mathcal O}(1)$ as given in Eqs.(\ref{ciqlBql}-\ref{iqlBdql}). Now we consider $\Pi^{5/3}_{a}$ is produced by $e$ and $u$ of the first family, and the branching ratio of decaying to $\tau$ and $t$ of the third family. The Yukawa coupling $g_Y\sim {\mathcal O}(1)$ for $e$ and $u$ production, and another Yukawa coupling $g'_Y$ for decaying to $\tau$ and $t$. The Yukawa coupling $g'_Y$ is a new parameter and $g'_Y < g_Y$, possibly $g'_Y\ll g_Y$ for the following reasons. The left- and right-handed fields of leptons and quarks, which make composite bosons and fermions, are the SM gauge eigenstates in each generation. They are the same as the mass eigenstates without considering generation mixing. If we need to consider the mixing, see the unitary flavour transformations eqs (15,16) for quarks and eqs (23, 24) for leptons in my article JHEP 2016 ref. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1605.01266.pdf. Using these unitary transformations $U^{\nu,\ell, u,d}_{L,R}$, we can rewrite the Yukawa couplings (\ref{ciqlB})-(\ref{iqlBdql}) by associating two unitary matrices $(U)^\dagger U$ which are unknown. As example,  by interacting (\ref{ciqlBql}) the $e$ and $u$ produced $\Pi_a^{5/3}$ will decay to $\tau$ and $t$ by interacting
512: \begin{eqnarray}
513: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{+5/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(U^\dagger_R U_L) (\bar \tau_{R}t_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.} = g'_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar \tau_{R}t_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.} ,\label{ciqlBqlmix}
514: \end{eqnarray}
515: where $g'_{_{\rm Y}} = g_{_{\rm Y}}(U^\dagger_R U_L)$, 
516: and the notation $(U^\dagger_R U_L)$ stands for relevant unitary transformations between generations considered. The general mixing matrix $(U^\dagger_R U_L)$ of leptoquark sector, see eq (35) of my JHEP 2016, has its analogies CKM matrix in quark sector, PMNS matrix in lepton sector. In conclusion, the general mixing matrix $(U^\dagger_R U_L)$ is totally unknown, the effective way for dealing with composite states of different generations but the same SM quantum numbers is to introduce a new Yukawa coupling. These discussions also apply to the three nonLQ composite bosons $\Pi^-$, $\Pi^0_u$ and $\Pi^0_d$ see eqs. (\ref{ciqlB})-(\ref{iqlBd}). It can be considered as a general rule for considering the initial and final states are not in the same family.}

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

# A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
NumberStr = str


class Rule(BaseModel):
    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""

    lhs: str
    rhs: str
    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"

    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"

    External = "External"
    Internal = "Internal"


class SpinType(str, Enum):
    S = "S"  # scalar
    F = "F"  # fermion
    V = "V"  # vector
    U = "U"  # ghost
    T = "T"  # tensor
    W = "W"  # Weyl fermion
    R = "R"  # spin-3/2
    RW = "RW"

    Unfold = "Unfold"
    NoUnfold = "NoUnfold"
    Range = "Range"


class PropType(str, Enum):
    Sine = "Sine"
    Straight = "Straight"
    ScalarDash = "ScalarDash"
    GhostDash = "GhostDash"
    Curly = "Curly"
    W = "W"
    C = "C"
    S = "S"

    true = "True"
    false = "False"

class GaugeGroup(BaseModel):

    gauge_boson: str
    coupling_constant: Optional[str] = None
    charge: Optional[str] = None  # required iff abelian
    structure_constant: Optional[str] = None  # required iff non-abelian
    symmetric_tensor: Optional[str] = None
    representations: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # [("T","Colour")] or many
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM rule strings

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "GaugeGroup":

            raise ValueError(f"gauge group {self.name}: Abelian group needs charge")

    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # scalar; tensors use value_rules
    value_rules: List[Rule] = []  # tensor Value -> { ... }
    complex: Optional[bool] = None  # ComplexParameter
    block_name: Optional[str] = None  # External only
    order_block: Optional[int] = None  # External SCALAR only
    interaction_order: Optional[Tuple[str, int]] = None  # -> {NP, 1}
    indices: List[str] = []  # non-empty => tensor
    definitions: List[Rule] = []
    parameter_name: Optional[str] = None
    tex: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    tensor_class: Optional[str] = None

    unitary: Optional[bool] = None
    hermitian: Optional[bool] = None
    orthogonal: Optional[bool] = None
    allow_summation: Optional[bool] = None

    @property
    def is_tensor(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.indices)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "Parameter":

            if self.value is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: tensor uses value_rules, not scalar value"
                )
            if self.order_block is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: order_block forbidden on tensors"
                )
        exclusive = [f for f in (self.unitary, self.hermitian, self.orthogonal) if f]
        if len(exclusive) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: at most one of unitary/hermitian/orthogonal"
            )
        if (self.unitary or self.hermitian) and self.complex is False:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: unitary/hermitian require complex=True"
            )
        if self.orthogonal and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(f"parameter {self.name}: orthogonal must be real")
        if self.parameter_type == ParamType.External and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: External params must be real "

    width: Optional[MassSpec] = None
    quantum_numbers: Dict[str, NumberStr] = {}  # values are strings -> preserve -1/3
    pdg: Optional[Union[int, List[int]]] = None
    particle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    antiparticle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    full_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_label: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_type: Optional[PropType] = None
    propagator_arrow: Optional[PropArrow] = None
    unphysical: bool = False
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM Mathematica rule strings
    ghost: Optional[str] = None  # U[n] only
    goldstone: Optional[str] = None  # S[n] only
    weyl_components: List[str] = []
    majorana_phase: Optional[str] = None
    chirality: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def class_label(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.spin_type.value}[{self.class_index}]"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "ParticleClass":

                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields omit mass/pdg"

    if not text:

    texts: List[str] = []
    if p.value:
        texts.append(p.value)
    for r in p.value_rules:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    for r in p.definitions:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    blob = " ".join(texts)
    return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}


def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
    """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.

    Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
    dependency cycle.
    """
    names = {p.name for p in params}
    deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
    by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}

    ordered: List[Parameter] = []
    emitted: set = set()
    remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order

    while remaining:
        progressed = False
        still: List[str] = []
        for n in remaining:
            if deps[n] <= emitted:
                ordered.append(by_name[n])
                emitted.add(n)
                progressed = True
            else:
                still.append(n)
        remaining = still
        if not progressed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
            )
    return ordered


class FeynRulesModel(BaseModel):
    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""

    model_name: str
    info: ModelInfo
    interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")

        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
        builtin = {
            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
        }
        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
        return self

## Important Details
- Working dir: `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-NJLComposite-zxkbktvj/` — work only inside it.
- Shell restricted: only `./frgen *` / `./frgen` allowed (all other bash denied). Use read/grep/write tools for everything else.
- Schema rules: numeric values are strings ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups: []`; standard indices (Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W) need no declaration; other indices need `index_decls` (range_kind "NoUnfold"); unique `class_index` ≥ 100; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields.
- Scoring: COMPLETENESS of new particles, External parameters, verbatim Mathematica `lagrangian_terms`.
- First `./frgen spec.json` run: SCHEMA OK (19 classes, 5 params, 26 terms), RENDERED `model.fr` (429 lines), LINT reported 13 findings (12 warn + 1 mg5). Fix plan per finding:
  - `explicit_index_in_dc` (warn, 6×): rewrite scalar kin as `ExpandIndices[DC[PI1bar, mu] DC[PI1, mu] - mPi^2 PI1bar[ii] PI1[ii], FlavorExpand->SU2D]` (no explicit index inside DC). Affects PI1, PI2, Hc1, Hc2, LQ1, LQ2 (model.fr lines 379–389).
  - `fieldless_term` (mg5) `LFCI` (model.fr line 423): lint `field_tokens` = class_names | class_name+"bar" | SM_FIELDS_ALL | bare ClassMembers (members get NO "bar" suffix; `\bFU0\b` doesn't match `FU0bar`). SM_FIELDS_ALL comes from `~/Documents/Github/heptapod/tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr` (missing locally ⇒ empty). Fix: rewrite using class fields with explicit SU2 indices: `FU1bar[sp1,1,ff,cc]` = bar U0, `FU1bar[sp1,2,ff,cc]` = bar U+ (antiparticle of FUm), `FD1bar` likewise; drop invalid `FUpb`/`FDpb`.
  - `undeclared_symbol FUpb` (warn): real — replace with `FU1bar[...,2,...]`.
  - `undeclared_symbol Eqs` (warn, LANOMPI0/LANOMPIc): real — strip all prose from expressions, move to `description`.
  - `undeclared_symbol QL` (warn, LYPI/LYLQ/LHcFF): false positive — external heptapod SM.fr missing locally; local `SM.fr` declares `QL`. Keep QL.
- FR projector conventions (from local SM.fr): `uR :> ProjP uq` (ProjP = RIGHT-handed), `LL[sp,1] :> ProjM.vl` (ProjM = LEFT). Derived bilinear forms: `bar(U_L) u_R` = `FU1bar.ProjP.uR` (since bar(U_L) = bar U P_R = barU ProjP); `bar(u_R) ν_L` = `uRbar.vl` (both chiral classes, FR handles contraction, like SM's `LLbar.lR Phi` pattern). Avoid stacking `ProjM.uR` (= ProjM ProjP = 0).
- Hypercharge audit: LYPI already Y=0 term-by-term (`dRbar QL[1] PIm`: 1/3+1/6−1/2=0; `dRbar QL[2] PI0dbar`; `uRbar QL[1] PI0ubar`; `uRbar CKM dq Pip`). Q sums also verified 0. LYLQ NOT yet Y=0: `eRbar QL[1] LQ53` = 1+1/6+7/6 = 2 ✗; fix by using LQ conjugates: `eRbar QL[1] LQ53bar` (Y=0), matching pion pattern (bilinear Y = Y(positive particle), pair with negative-particle field / conjugate). Paper writes Π^{+5/3} literally but gauge invariance requires the conjugate — document in description/audit.
- `vyR` (used in LYLQ ν terms) is NOT in SM and undeclared — replace with declared sterile `nur`: e.g. `nurbar QL[2] LQm13bar` (0+1/6−1/6=0).
- `Nc`: grep of spec.json for `Nc ==|Nc ->` found NOTHING; local SM.fr parameters section (lines 460+) shows no Nc either ⇒ Nc undeclared. Either add an Internal parameter `Nc == {ParameterType->Internal, Value->3}` or fold Nc=3 into numeric anomaly coefficients.
- Anomaly term structure (paper PiGG, tex ~922–941): L = (g g' Nc)/(4 π² F_Π) ε (∂A)(∂A') Π0(+ h.c. for charged). Use `Eps[mu,nu,rho,sig] FS[...] FS[...]`. Explicit coefficients (with the paper's 1/4 for F-form): Π0u γγ: `ee^2/(12 Pi^2 FPi)` (g=g'=2/3 ee, Nc=3); Π0d γγ: `ee^2/(48 Pi^2 FPi)`; gg: `(gs^2/2)/(4 Pi^2 FPi)`; charged γW: `ee gw/(12 Sqrt[2] Pi^2 FPi)`. Neutral components: Π0u = `PI2[1]`, Π0d = `PI1[2]`. Do NOT declare `gQ2` — write coefficients explicitly. Interaction-order lint satisfied because FPi carries {NP,-1}.
- Contact Yukawa Eqs. (ciqlB–iqlBdql, tex 488–501) and composite-fermion contact (cieFf0+ etc., tex 818–831) confirmed by re-read; composite fermion constituent table (tex 693–708): U0_R = u_R(ū_R ν_L), Q=0 t3=1/2 Y=−1/2; U−_R Y=−1/2 t3=−1/2; D0_R/D−_R analogous — colour-singlet, repeat colour index summed, no gluon coupling at leading order.

- Naming constraints: avoid SM.fr/FR-symbol collisions (`Pi`, `N`, `D`, `E`, `HC`, `DC`, ...) — hence PI1/Hc1/FN1 style; no primes/punctuation in ParticleName.
- Lint internals (`tools/fr_lint.py`): `term_defs` stops at `^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)`; undeclared check fires only for uppercase-starting identifiers used with `[` or `.`; `FR_SYMBOLS`/`PROTECTED` name-collision sets; `sm_couplings = {"ee","gw","gs","g1","yl","yu","yd","lam","CKM"}`.
- SM.fr classes confirmed: `vl{ve,vm,vt}`, `l{e,mu,ta}`, `uq{u,c,t}`, `dq{d,s,b}`, `LL`, `lR`, `QL`, `uR`, `dR`, `H`, `G0`, `GP`, `Phi`, gauge/ghost classes.

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.
3: 
4: Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
5: MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
6: repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
7: predicts takes up to 900 s.
8: 
9: Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import json
22: import re
23: import sys
24: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
25: from pathlib import Path
26: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
27: 
28: HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
29: SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"
30: 
31: # Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}
39: 
40: # Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
42: SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
43: SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
44: for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
45:     SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
46: _i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
47: SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
48: SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
49: SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
50:               "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
51: SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
52: SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
53:              "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}
54: 
55: FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
56:                "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
57:                "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
58:                "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
59:                "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
60:                "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
61:                "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
62:                "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
63:                "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
64:                "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}
65: 
66: 
67: @dataclass
68: class Finding:
69:     rule: str
70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None
73: 
74: 
75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1
109: 
110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None
157: 
158: 
159: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- lints
160: 
161: def lint_text(raw: str) -> List[Finding]:
162:     text = strip_comments(raw)
163:     F: List[Finding] = []
164:     classes = _entries(_block(text, "ClassesDescription"))
165:     params = _entries(_block(text, "Parameters"))
166:     terms = term_defs(text)
167:     term_names = {t["name"] for t in terms}
168:     term_bodies = "\n".join(t["body"] for t in terms)
169: 
170:     class_names, class_idx = {}, {}
171:     for c in classes:
172:         cn = _prop(c["body"], "ClassName")
173:         if cn:
174:             class_names[cn] = c
175:             mi = re.match(r"(\w+)\[\s*(\d+)\s*\]", c["head"])
176:             if mi:
177:                 class_idx[cn] = (mi.group(1), int(mi.group(2)))
178:     param_names = {p["head"]: p for p in params}
179:     index_decls = dict(re.findall(r"IndexRange\[\s*Index\[(\w+)\]\s*\]\s*=\s*([^;\n]+)", text))
180: 
181:     # --- rule 10: names -------------------------------------------------
182:     for name in list(class_names) + list(param_names) + list(index_decls):
183:         if name in FR_SYMBOLS:
184:             F.append(Finding("feynrules_symbol_name", "compile",
185:                              f"`{name}` is a FeynRules symbol", _line_of(text, name)))
186:         elif name in PROTECTED:
187:             F.append(Finding("protected_name", "warn",
188:                              f"`{name}` is a Mathematica built-in (loads with a warning; renaming is safer)",
189:                              _line_of(text, name)))
190:     for name in class_names:
191:         if name in SM_CLASSES or name in SM_MEMBERS:
192:             F.append(Finding("sm_class_redeclared", "warn",
193:                              f"class `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr (doubly-defined class)",
194:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {name}")))
195:     for name in param_names:
196:         if name in SM_PARAMS or name in SM_MASSES:
197:             F.append(Finding("sm_parameter_redeclared", "warn",
198:                              f"parameter `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr", _line_of(text, name)))
199:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
200:         for key in ("ParticleName", "AntiParticleName"):
201:             v = _prop(c["body"], key)
202:             names = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', v) if v else []
203:             if v and any(re.search(r"[\'`\s!@#%^&*()=\[\]{}|\\;:<>?/,]", nm) for nm in names):
204:                 F.append(Finding("bad_particle_name", "mg5",
205:                                  f"class `{cn}`: {key} {v} is not a valid UFO identifier", _line_of(text, v)))
206:         if cn in class_idx and class_idx[cn][1] < 100:
207:             F.append(Finding("low_class_index", "warn",
208:                              f"class `{cn}` uses index {class_idx[cn][0]}[{class_idx[cn][1]}]; SM.fr uses the low indices",
209:                              _line_of(text, c["head"])))
210:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
211:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
212:                 if mem in SM_MEMBERS or mem in SM_CLASSES:
213:                     F.append(Finding("sm_member_redeclared", "compile",
214:                                      f"class member `{mem}` of `{cn}` collides with an SM.fr name",
215:                                      _line_of(text, mem)))
216:     if "$" in re.sub(r"M\$\w+", "", text):
217:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b\w*\$\w*", text):
218:             if not re.match(r"^(M|MR|FR)\$", m.group(0)):
219:                 F.append(Finding("dollar_in_name", "mg5", f"`{m.group(0)}` contains `$` (invalid Python)",
220:                                  text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1))
221:                 break
222: 
223:     # --- rule 11: interaction orders --------------------------------------
224:     hierarchy = _block(text, "InteractionOrderHierarchy")
225:     orders_declared = set(re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*-?\d+\s*\}", hierarchy))
226:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
227:         body = p["body"]
228:         ptype = (_prop(body, "ParameterType") or "External").strip()
229:         io = _prop(body, "InteractionOrder")
230:         used = re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", term_bodies) is not None
231:         is_mass = any(re.search(rf"Mass\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"]) or
232:                       re.search(rf"Width\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"])
233:                       for c in classes) or re.match(r"^(M|W)[A-Z]", pn) and not io
234:         if io:
235:             oname = re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,", io)
236:             for o in oname:
237:                 if o not in orders_declared and o not in ("QCD", "QED"):
238:                     F.append(Finding("order_not_in_hierarchy", "warn",
239:                                      f"parameter `{pn}` uses InteractionOrder `{o}` not listed in M$InteractionOrderHierarchy",
240:                                      _line_of(text, pn)))
241:     ordered = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items() if _prop(p["body"], "InteractionOrder")}
242:     internal = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items()
243:                 if (_prop(p["body"], "ParameterType") or "External").strip() == "Internal"}
244:     # an Internal parameter inherits the orders of the parameters in its Value
245:     for pn in list(internal):
246:         val = _prop(param_names[pn]["body"], "Value") or ""
247:         if any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(o)}\b", val) for o in ordered):
248:             ordered.add(pn)
249:     for t in terms:
250:         if _is_kin_name(t["name"]):
251:             continue
252:         used_params = {pn for pn in param_names if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", t["body"])}
253:         sm_couplings = {"ee", "gw", "gs", "g1", "yl", "yu", "yd", "lam", "CKM"}
254:         if used_params and not (used_params & ordered) and not \
255:                 any(re.search(rf"\b{c}\b", t["body"]) for c in sm_couplings) and \
256:                 not any(re.search(rf"\b(DC|FS)\[", t["body"]) for _ in [0]):
257:             F.append(Finding("missing_interaction_order", "mg5",
258:                              f"`{t['name']}`: none of its parameters ({', '.join(sorted(used_params))}) carries an InteractionOrder",
259:                              t["line"]))
260: 
261:     # --- rule 12: pattern rules on tensor parameters -----------------------
262:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
263:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:?->", p["body"]) or "_?NumericQ" in p["body"]:
264:             F.append(Finding("pattern_rule_definition", "mg5",
265:                              f"parameter `{pn}` uses a pattern rule in Definitions/Value; FeynRules exports it verbatim as a UFO name",
266:                              _line_of(text, pn)))
267:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
268:         d = _prop(c["body"], "Definitions") or ""
269:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:>", d) and not re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_\s*[,\]]", d):
270:             pass  # `X[mu_] :> ...` is the normal FeynRules idiom; leave it
271: 
272:     # --- rule 13: explicit indices ------------------------------------------
273:     for t in terms:
274:         b = t["body"]
275:         for m in re.finditer(r"DC\[\s*(\w+)\[([^\]]*)\]\s*,", b):
276:             fld = m.group(1)
277:             c = class_names.get(fld)
278:             idx = (_prop(c["body"], "Indices") or "") if c else ""
279:             if c and re.search(r"Colour|Sextet|Gluon|Octet|Col", idx):
280:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "compile",
281:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on `{fld}` with an explicit colour-type index", t["line"]))
282:             else:
283:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "warn",
284:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on an explicitly indexed field `{fld}`", t["line"]))
285:             break
286:         if re.search(r"Index\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]\s*,\s*Index\[\s*Generation", b) or \
287:                 re.search(r"\w+\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]", b):
288:             F.append(Finding("nested_generation_index", "compile",
289:                              f"`{t['name']}`: nested generation index", t["line"]))
290:         m = re.search(r"\b(\w+)\[\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|ii\d?)\s*,\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|jj\d?)\s*\]\s*\w+bar\[", b)
291:         if m and m.group(1) in param_names:
292:             F.append(Finding("explicit_flavour_sum", "mg5",
293:                              f"`{t['name']}`: flavour matrix `{m.group(1)}` with explicit generation indices instead of matrix form",
294:                              t["line"]))

Run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate as described under TOOLKIT. Your final message: the self-audit table and one line with the last ./frgen result. spec.json as it is on disk when you stop is rendered and scored.

Model file this add-on is loaded on top of: take field names, index conventions and
hypercharges from it), the schema tools/frgen/frmodel.py, the renderer

## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
   - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
   - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
   - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.

4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.

5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:

A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
   - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.

263: \section{Four-fermion operators and contact interactions}\label{contact}
264: 
265: The SM parity-violating (chiral) gauge symmetries and spontaneous/explicit breaking of these symmetries for the $W$ and $Z$ gauge boson 
266: masses and the hierarchy pattern of fermion masses have been at the 
267: centre of conceptual elaboration for possible scenarios beyond. The No-Go theorem \cite{Nielsen:1981xu, 1981PhLB..105..219N} shows that as a renormalizable quantum field theory at infrared (IR) low energies, the SM {\it bilinear} fermion Lagrangian at ultraviolet (UV) cutoff $\Lambda_{\rm cut}$ suffers theoretical inconsistencies with SM chiral gauge symmetries and fermion spectra at low energies. 
268: It implies that the BSM Lagrangian at $\Lambda_{\rm cut}$ should have {\it quadrilinear} operators \cite{Xue:2016dpl, Xue2017}
269: \begin{eqnarray}
270: \sum_{f=1,2,3}G_{\rm cut}\, \Big[\bar\psi^{f}_{_L}\psi^{f}_{_R}\bar\psi^{f}_{_R} \psi^{f}_{_L}\Big]_{q=0,-1,2/3,-1/3},\quad G_{\rm cut}\propto \Lambda^{-2}_{\rm cut},
271: \label{q1}
272: \end{eqnarray}
273: which is SM gauge symmetric four-fermion interactions of left- and right-handed fermions ($\psi^f_L,\psi^f_R$) in the SM charge sector ``$q$'' and flavour family ``$f$''. They are four-fermion operators of Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) or Einstein-Cartan type. Their origins at the scale $\Lambda_{\rm cut}$ are due to unknown grand unified interaction or quantum gravity dynamics.  
274: 
275: The strong four-fermion coupling $g_{\rm cut }\propto G_{\rm cut}\Lambda^2_{\rm cut}$ dynamics leads to composite bosons $\Pi^{f}\sim (\bar\psi^{f}_{_R} \psi^{f}_{_L})$ and fermions $F^{f}_R\sim \psi^{f}_{_R} (\bar\psi^{f}_{_R} \psi^{f}_{_L})\sim \psi^{f}_{_R}\Pi^{f}$ \cite{Xue1996, Xue2000, Xue2000a}. They 
276: are represented by the
277: mass (pole) and form factor (residue) of propagators, behaving as elementary particles after form-factor renormalisation. These composite particles carry SM quantum numbers and couple to massless SM gauge bosons. Their massive spectra preserve SM gauge symmetries, and constituents can 
278: be leptons, quarks or leptoquarks. There exists a UV fixed point $g^*_{\rm cut}$ and scaling domain, which realises an SM gauge symmetric, renormalizable {\it bilinear and dimensional-4} Lagrangian of composite bosons and fermions at the composite scale $\Lambda\ll \Lambda_{\rm cut}$ \cite{Xue2014, Xue2017}. 
279: As the energy scale decreases below $\Lambda$, the effective theory undergoes \cite{Xue2023} a phase transition of composite particles decay into constituents and spontaneous SM symmetries breaking via the top-quark channel $(\bar t_Lt_R\bar t_R t_L)$, realising the $\bar tt$-composite Higgs boson  
280: at the electroweak scale $v\approx 246$ GeV \cite{Bardeen1990}. The scale $\Lambda\approx 5.1$ TeV is estimated by using the top quark and Higgs boson masses and extrapolating the renormalization-group solution to the high-energy regime \cite{Xue2013}.
281: 
282: In this section we describe the four-fermion operators and contact interactions that are relevant for the study of the phenomenology of the composite bosons at $pp$ or $ep$  collisions, 
283: including the LHC, which will be detailed in Sec.~\ref{PhenomenologyCompositeFermions}.
284: 
285: We consider, among four-fermion operators (\ref{q1}) in introduction, the following SM gauge-symmetric and fermion-number conserving four-fermion operators, 
286: \begin{eqnarray}
287: &&G\left[(\bar\ell^{i}_Le_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})
288: +(\bar\ell^{i}_L\nu^e_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})\right] + {\rm h.c.},
289: \label{bhlql}
290: \end{eqnarray}
291: and
292: \begin{eqnarray}
293: &&G\left[(\bar\ell^{i}_L\nu^e_{R})(\bar \nu^e_{R}\ell_{Li})
294: +(\bar\ell^{i}_Le_{R})(\bar e_{R}\ell_{Li})\right]+ {\rm h.c.}\nonumber\\
295: &&G\left[(\bar\ell^{i}_Lu^a_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}\ell_{Li})
296: +(\bar\ell^{i}_Ld^a_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}\ell_{Li})\right]+ {\rm h.c.}
297: \label{bhlql1}
298: \end{eqnarray}
299: and
300: \begin{eqnarray}
301: &&G\left[(\bar\psi_{Lia}\nu^e_{R})(\bar \nu^e_{R}\psi_{Lia})
302: +(\bar\psi_{Lia}e_{R})(\bar e_{R}\psi_{Lia})\right] + {\rm h.c.},
303: \label{bhlql2}\\
304: &&G\left[(\bar\psi^{bi}_Lu_{Rb})(\bar u^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})+(\bar\psi^{bi}_Ld_{Rb})(\bar d^a_{R}\psi_{Lia})\right] + {\rm h.c.},
305: \label{qbhlql}
306: \end{eqnarray}
307: being the SM doublet $\ell^i_L=(\nu^e_L,e_L)$ and singlet $e_{R}$ with an additional right-handed neutrino $\nu^e_{R}$ for leptons;
308: $\psi_{Lia}=(u_{La},d_{La})$ and $u^a_{R}, d^a_{R}$ for quarks, 
309: where the color $a,b$ and $SU_L(2)$-isospin $i$ indexes are summed over.
310: Eqs. (\ref{bhlql})-(\ref{qbhlql}) 
311: are for the first family only, as a representative of the three fermion families.
312: The SM left- and right-handed fermions are mass eigenstates, their masses are negligible 
313: in TeV-energy regime and small mixing among three families encoded 
314: in $G$ is also neglected \cite{xue2016_2}.

320: \label{bhlqlex}\\
321: &&G\left[(\bar\nu^e_Lu^a_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}\nu^e_{L})+
322: (\bar e_Lu^a_{R})(\bar u^a_{R}e_{L})
323: +(\bar\nu^e_Ld^a_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}\nu^e_{L})+
324: (\bar e_Ld^a_{R})(\bar d^a_{R}e_{L})\right] + {\rm h.c.},\nonumber\\

327: +(\bar d^a_L e_{R})(\bar e_{R}d^a_{L})\right] + {\rm h.c.},\nonumber

482: \subsection{Contact interaction of composite bosons, quarks and leptons}\label{spqq}
483: 
484: As shown in Fig.~\ref{compositeBv}, 
485: the effective coupling between composite boson 
486: and its two constituents can be written as an effective contact interaction, 
487: \begin{eqnarray}
488: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^\pm}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar d^a_{R}u_{La})\Pi^- + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlB}\\
489: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_d}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar d^a_{R} d_{La})\Pi^0_d + {\rm h.c.},
490: \label{iqlBd}\\
491: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^0_u}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar u^a_{R} u_{La})\Pi^0_u + {\rm h.c.},
492: \label{iqlBu}
493: \end{eqnarray}
494: and 
495: \begin{eqnarray}
496: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{+5/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R}u_{La})\Pi^{+5/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql}\\
497: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{-1/3}_a}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar\nu^e_{R}d_{La})\Pi^{-1/3}_a + {\rm h.c.},\label{ciqlBql1}\\
498: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}} (\bar \nu^e_{R}u_{La}) \Pi^{2/3}_{u_a} + {\rm h.c.},
499: \label{iqlBuql}\\
500: {\mathcal L}^{\rm \Pi^{2/3}_{d_a}}_{\rm CI} &=& g_{_{\rm Y}}(\bar e_{R} d_{La})\Pi^{2/3}_{d_a} + {\rm h.c.},
501: \label{iqlBdql}
502: \end{eqnarray}
503: where $g_{_{\rm Y}}=(F_\Pi/\Lambda)^2$.
504: Appropriate normalizing the composite boson $\Pi$ with the 
505: form factor $(g^*/F_\Pi)^2$ in Eqs. (\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}),  
506: the effective contact interaction in Eqs. (\ref{ciqlB}-\ref{iqlBu}) and (\ref{ciqlBql}-\ref{iqlBdql}) can be expressed as a dimensionless Yukawa coupling $g_{_{\rm Y}}$, 
507: whose value, corresponding to $F_\Pi$ value, 
508: can be different for composite bosons in Eqs.~(\ref{nB0}-\ref{uB0}) and (\ref{nB5/3}-\ref{uB2/3}), but we do not consider such difference here.
509: These are relevant contact interactions for phenomenological studies of possible inelastic channels of composite-fermion production and decay in  $pp$ or $ep$ collisions.
